- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots — cap forecast at +5% above prior high or use 30-day moving average.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model often fails to recognize mean reversion — adjust downward by 2–5% for 3–5 days ahead.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to overestimate short-term volatility — smooth forecast with 14-day EWMA.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days) — apply 3–5% downward bias to first 7 days.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from -0.5 to +0.5 in 3–5 days), model lags — add 1–2% upward bias to forecast 3–5 days ahead.
